 SALT LAKE CITY (KUTV) — Two youth-oriented vehicles recalled by the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission on November 5 could pose crash hazards.
 U.S. Titan is recalling about 117 X-Pro Eagle youth all-terrain vehicles because the included speed-adjusting module can let the ATV exceed the maximum speed allowed for vehicles intended for children six and older. The gas-powered, 110cc ATVs were sold online at Walmart.com, Powersportsmax.com, Xprousa.com, Amazon.com and eBay from July through September 2025 for $680 to $980.
 Consumers should stop using the speed-adjusting module and contact X-Pro for a $100 refund. The ATV can still be used without the module, which customers will be asked to return with a prepaid shipping label. No incidents or injuries have been reported.

 Sanven Technology is recalling about 1,950 black Vevor BMX bicycles because they lack a chain guard. Loose clothing could become caught in the chain drive, creating a risk of serious injury or a deadly crash. 
 The recall covers 20- and 24-inch bicycles, models SS24001 and SS24002, sold at Vevor stores nationwide and online at Vevor.com from October 2024 through April 2026 for $152 to $188.
 Consumers should stop using the bikes and contact Sanven Technology for a free repair kit with a chain guard and installation instructions. No incidents or injuries have been reported.
